sections.h2: Register of Deeds office and what it does
sections.html:
The Blount County Register of Deeds is at 349 Court Street, Maryville, TN 37804. The phone number is 865-273-5880, and the doors are open weekdays from 8 a.m. until 4:30 p.m.

Think of it as a filing counter. The staff will not search a title, hand you forms or draft a document. Sellers in Blount County usually get the deed from a title company or real estate attorney, and the register files it after the tax has been paid.

The seat of the county, and its biggest city, is Maryville. Alcoa, Friendsville, Rockford and Townsend are cities as well, and Louisville is a town. Tennessee records land county by county, so all of these addresses are handled at the same Court Street counter.

Before closing day, ask the title company whether it will e-record or deliver a paper original. A paper deed needs the fees paid up front and an envelope if you want the original sent back, while e-recording goes through one of the approved vendors. Either way, ask for the recording information afterward and keep it with your sale papers, since you will need the book and page reference if the deed is ever referred to again.

The July 2025 estimate puts Blount County at 143,820 people living in 64,682 housing units, of which 77.0 percent are owner-occupied. Typical value for an owner-occupied home was $320,500 over 2020 to 2024. Public schools are run by Blount County Schools, except in Maryville and Alcoa, which have their own systems. School district, city limits and proximity to park land all vary by address, so confirm the parcel's jurisdiction before you list.

Recording a document of one or two pages is $12. Every additional page or attachment adds $5, and any document with a taxable amount, like a warranty deed or deed of trust, also gets a $1 clerk fee.

Document or serviceCounty fee
Recording, one or two pages$12
Additional page or attachment$5
Clerk fee on documents with a taxable amount$1
Extra reference on documents other than deeds and trust deeds$5 per reference after the first
Certified copy of a recorded document$1 per page ($5 for maps)
Transfer tax on a deed$0.37 per $100
Mortgage tax$0.115 per $100, first $2,000 exempt

Pay when you file. Cash, check, credit or debit card and money order all work. Because page count drives the fee, have the register confirm the total in advance whenever your deed comes with attachments.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on a home sale
sections.html:
Under Tennessee law each $100 of the price, or of the value if higher, carries $0.37 in tax. Legally the buyer named as grantee owes it, and the register takes payment as the deed is filed.

When the buyer finances, a mortgage tax applies too, at $0.115 per $100 for everything borrowed past the first $2,000. Purchase agreements sometimes shift these costs, so look at yours.

In front of the register, the grantee swears on the deed's face to the real consideration or the value, taking the larger number. Lying about value can be prosecuted as perjury. State reviewers also line deed values up against assessor values, and a suspiciously low price can bring an inquiry letter.

Expect the counter to reject a deed that lacks any of these county requirements.

  • A Prepared By line, with name and address, on each document.
  • District, map and parcel number, plus name and address for both the owner and the responsible taxpayer.
  • Book and page references in a format such as WD508 Pg 61. The office cannot reference documents by instrument number.
  • On trust deeds, mortgages, modifications and assignments, the sentence: 'Maximum principal indebtedness for Tennessee recording tax purposes is $____.' Even a zero amount must be written.
  • A self-addressed stamped envelope if you want the original returned, which the office does for real estate documents after recording.

A recorded error cannot be corrected by hand. Recording the document again needs new signatures and a notary, unless you file a scrivener's error affidavit that refers to the earlier document and states the correction. If the owner is wrong, a new deed must be prepared and filed.

The state recordation tax manual names transfers that owe no realty transfer tax. Several are common in family and estate sales, and none needs an oath of consideration.

  • Leasehold estate transfers.
  • A spouse conveying to the other to create or end a tenancy by the entirety.
  • An executor's deed carrying out a devise in a will.
  • Divorce decrees and deeds that settle property between the spouses.
  • Moves into or out of a revocable living trust by the same person or spouse.
  • Dealings with a government entity.

Quitclaim deeds are taxed on the consideration given. But if the language, such as 'in fee simple' or 'to have and to hold', shows the grantor meant to convey the property itself, fair market value is the base. Ask the title agent which way yours will be read.

Deed records are not on the county website. Public computers at 349 Court Street let you search in person. Online access runs through a vendor, US Title Search Network (ustitlesearch.net, 615-223-1823), and you contact that company to subscribe.

E-recording comes in through Simplifile (800-460-5657) or CSC (1-866-403-5272). Copies cost $0.50 to email each document or $0.50 per page to print. Certified copies that serve as an original are $1.00 per page. An independent service called CRS (Courthouse Retrieval) is not run by the county or the register, so errors in its data go to that company.

The register does not track foreclosure sales posted on the courthouse steps. When a lender sale is pending on your house, the lender or its trustee has the schedule. A title agency can verify what is recorded on the parcel.

sections.h2: Getting a Blount County sale to the register
sections.html:
The sequence is brief. A title company or attorney drafts the deed with the parcel number and addresses described above. The buyer takes the oath of value, and tax and fees are paid on recording. Payoffs and old liens get cleared by the title company beforehand.

A house that needs repairs, or one tied up in an unfinished estate, can be sold to us as-is. We pay cash for Blount County houses, and the deed still goes through this office under identical rules. Gather the previous deed, your tax bill and payoff figures first.

faqs.q: What is the phone number for the Blount County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The line is 865-273-5880. Visit 349 Court Street, Maryville, TN 37804 on weekdays between 8 a.m. and 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: How much does Blount County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: Expect $12 for the first two pages, $5 for each page after that, and $1 more for documents with a taxable amount. A sale also carries the $0.37 per $100 transfer tax.

faqs.q: Who pays the Tennessee transfer tax on a house sale?
faqs.a: By law the buyer named on the deed owes it. Your contract can still split the cost another way.

faqs.q: Can I look up Blount County deeds online?
faqs.a: Only through a vendor. Searchers are sent to ustitlesearch.net, which needs a subscription. Free computers are available at 349 Court Street.

faqs.q: Does the Blount County register prepare my deed or check my title?
faqs.a: No. The office records documents only. A title company or attorney handles the deed and the title search.
